areas.assessment: Read, Project, Filter, Join, Set, Aggregate, Sort and Fetch cover the planned VTX2 logical core, but protobuf and individual semantics are still pre-1.0 and require a pinned profile.
Scalar, aggregate, window, cast and conditional concepts are present. Function declarations, signatures and extension identifiers continue to evolve and must be versioned with the plan profile.
Primitive, compound, nullable, variation and user-defined types exist. Timestamp, interval and UDT details still receive breaking or clarifying changes.

Substrait intentionally resolves fields structurally and positionally. DVT requires stable editable FieldId and RelationId across rename, reorder, reload and lineage, so direct persisted authoring requires a proven sidecar or a bounded authoring representation.

UNNEST and EXPLODE require cardinality-changing semantics still under active design around table functions or GenerateRel. They should fail closed or use a temporary extension, not a private silent interpretation.
Hash/merge joins, exchanges and physical aggregates do not block DVT semantic authoring because graphSource, Planner and ExecutionPlan remain the physical/runtime boundary.
Duplicated messages and deprecated fields are being normalized before 1.0. DVT can mitigate this only through exact version pins, compatibility fixtures and explicit migrations.

Exact equality across engines remains nuanced for ordering, decimals, nulls and implementation-specific behavior. DVT must retain target capabilities and provider-native validation even when a plan is valid Substrait.
The released validator targets substantially older spec versions than the current Python producer. Validation evidence must distinguish version incompatibility from an invalid plan.
Text representation completeness is useful for diagnostics but not required for the canonical binary plan boundary if protobuf JSON is treated only as evidence/debug output.

DVT is TypeScript-heavy. Generated protobuf bindings are possible, but maintained builders, inference and extension resolution are currently stronger in Python/Java/Rust than JavaScript. Integration cost must be measured rather than hidden behind wrappers.

DuckDB, DataFusion, Velox and other consumers exist, but producer/consumer spec lag can reject plans or even crash native integrations. Interoperability must be proven for the pinned profile and cannot be inferred from project logos.
JSON file read description is not yet core and implementations diverge. This does not block named relational tables in VTX2 but matters for future heterogeneous source plans.
